The cutoff exists since 0<m<=W. The mass below its shell is strictly below m by minimality, and the mass through it is at least m. Thus the equal shell mass is positive and at most a. The constructed uniform within-fiber densities are dominated and invariant under (z,x) to (-z,-x), which gives the full ambient zero first moment.

Subtracting r times the zero difference of the total masses gives the displayed cost difference. Each strict-shell term is nonnegative and vanishes exactly when its lower-shell mass is a or its upper-shell mass is zero. All equal-shell terms vanish. The comparison is valid even on the mass-only box, so it characterizes the optimum among the centroid-feasible measures irrespective of within-fiber densities.

Domination gives the upper cap bound. For a containing closed halfspace, writing its threshold with zero on the included side shows H and -H cover the ambient space. By symmetry they have equal selected mass, so each has at least m/2 even with mass on their overlap. With a nonzero continuous normal and zero threshold the overlap has d-volume zero in each fiber, which proves equality for that cap.

Independently computed n=1 with capacities divided by a. Radii 0,1,4 have multiplicities 1,2,2 and target mass 5/2, hence cutoff radius squared 1 and leftover 3/2. The base moment forces the two cutoff masses to equal 3/4. The objective is 3/2 in these units, or 3a/2. Exact shell enumeration through n=6 also checked the cutoff mass and capacity arithmetic.

For this product the whole C is a single closed winner cell with centroid zero and mass W. The hull of its single centroid base is the singleton {0}, and this cell charges every source fiber. This directly separates the two counts.
